title: RuneScape: Dragonwilds Update - SAVE FIXES, NEW COMBAT SKILLS & HUGE BUG FIXES!
author: NRS NEO
description:
RuneScape: Dragonwilds Update  - SAVE FIXES, NEW COMBAT SKILLS & HUGE BUG FIXES!

RuneScape: Dragonwilds just received a major update packed with important save fixes, exciting new combat abilities, quality of life improvements, and tons of bug fixes! 🔥

In this video, we're covering everything you need to know, including the fixes for disappearing world saves, the recovery option for corrupted character saves, and the new combat abilities that give ranged weapons more variety.

⚔️ What's included in this update?

✅ Fixes for disappearing world saves and corrupted character saves
✅ New Jump Attack ability with Death From Above
✅ New Shortbow, Longbow, and Crossbow special attacks
✅ Ammo Recovery and Greater Ammo Recovery perks
✅ Low Blow perk to slow down enemies
✅ Inventory capacity increased from 32 to 40 slots
✅ Dedicated Ring and Amulet equipment slots
✅ New Ultra Compost Bin and Large Compost Bucket
✅ Completed Quests tab and improved inventory sorting
✅ Enemy detection and respawn adjustments
✅ Scorned Wilderness Raid fixes and improvements
✅ Numerous combat, multiplayer, interface, performance, and quest bug fixes

We'll also look back at the previous update and explain how these latest save fixes build on the earlier work to help players get back into their worlds.

There's plenty to cover for anyone exploring Ashenfall, whether you're focused on combat, progression, resource gathering, or simply enjoying the adventure.

Let me know in the comments which change you're most excited about!

transcript.text: Hey, what's going on guys? My name is Nico Russell and we've got a pretty important RuneScape Dragon Wilds update
to go over. Let's start with the biggest concern, which is the save issues that players have been dealing with.
Losing access to your world is frustrating enough, but having your character save become corrupted on top
of that can make you feel like all those hours of gathering resources, fighting enemies, crafting equipment, and
progressing through the game have gone to waste. This update brings another round of fixes targeting those missing
world saves. And there's also a recovery option for players whose character saves
have been corrupted. Affected characters can get back into the game with aggregated stats and tier four gear,
giving them a way to continue playing instead of being completely locked out. Now, this doesn't necessarily mean every
lost detail of your previous progress will be restored, so keep that in mind. The team has also acknowledged that a
few unusual save problems may still exist, and they're continuing to collect to collect information on those cases.
Still, getting affected players back into their worlds and giving corrupted characters a way to return is probably
the most important part of this update. Now, moving over to combat to combat, we've got a new ability that sounds
pretty fun to use. It's called jump attack, and you unlock it through the skill tree perk named death from above.
The idea is exactly what you would expect. Once you're high enough above the ground, beyond the maximum height of
your normal double jump, you can attack and send your character plunging down onto an enemy below.
The damage depends on on the weapon you're holding, so the weapon you choose matters here.
You can also use wind step to set yourself up for the attack, which opens up some interesting possibilities for
combining movement abilities with combat. I can see this being particularly useful
when approaching a group of enemies from above, especially if you want to get the first hit in before things get messy.
Ranged combat has also received some attention, and there are some pretty meaningful changes for anyone who
prefers using bows or crossbows instead of getting up close with enemies. First, there are two new perks in the
ranged skill tree, ammo recovery and greater ammo recovery. These give you a chance to recover arrows from defeated
enemies, which could be useful during longer expeditions when you're running low on ammunition.
Having to constantly worry about your arrow supply can interrupt the flow of a fight, so being able to get some of
those arrows back is a welcome addition. On top of that, each each ranged weapon now has its own special attack. The
shortbow gets rapid fire, which lets you hop backwards and fire three arrows in quick succession.
What's nice here is that you can switch targets between those shots, allowing you to spread the damage across multiple
enemies instead of putting everything into one target. That gives the shortbow a more mobile play style, which should
suit players who like keeping their distance and moving around during combat. The longbow gets power shot, and this
one is much more about hitting hard from a distance. Your character takes a knee, draws the
arrow at full strength, and releases a powerful shot over long range. If you're trying to damage a dangerous enemy
before it gets close to you, this could be a great option. Then there's the crossbow, which gets
heavy bolt. You charge the shot briefly, release the bolt, and apply enchanted effects when it hits. So, rather than
giving every ranged weapon the same kind of attack, these abilities give each one a more distinct more distinct purpose.
There's also a new perk called low blow. When your ranged attacks hit an enemy in
the legs or the lower part of its body, you can apply hamstring, which reduces that enemy's movement speed for a short
time. That could make it easier to manage enemies that keep rushing toward you, especially when you're trying to
create some distance before firing again. Just remember that tiny and colossal enemies are immune to this effect, so it
won't work against absolutely everything you encounter. Moving away from combat, one One
favorite quality of life changes is the inventory expansion. The inventory now has 40 slots instead of 32.
That extra space should be useful when you're out gathering materials, exploring unfamiliar areas, or taking on
longer trips where you don't want to keep heading back to your base because your bags are full.
It isn't the only inventory improvement either because the sorting options have been improved. You can sort items by
weight, by type, or by the latest items you've picked up. Weight puts the heaviest cumulative
stacks first. Type organizes items alphabetically by category, and latest puts recently collected items at the front.
These options should make it easier to find what you need without manually moving everything around.
Equipment management is getting an improvement as well because rings and amulets now have their own dedicated
slots. That means you no longer have to treat those two equipment types as competing for the same space, which
should make organizing your character's gear more convenient. There has also been a balance adjustment
to the amulet of glory since it was providing bonuses beyond what was originally intended.
For players who enjoy farming and managing their base, there are a couple of additions here, too.
We've got the ultra compost bin, which takes things a step beyond the existing super compost bin, along with a large
compost bucket that can hold more material. The update also adds a completed quests
tab, including a short summary of each quest's outcome. That's a useful addition if you've been
playing for a while and want to look back at completed objectives without trying to remember every detail.
Another welcome change is the ability to toggle the visceral attack camera change. If you prefer having more
control over how combat looks and feels, that's a nice option to have. Overdrive can now also be cast on the
advanced spinning wheel, and the fishing cape should display its skill perk correctly, including the
chance to catch a fish instantly. There are some adjustments to the way enemies behave throughout the world, too.
Their detection range has been reduced, meaning they shouldn't notice you from quite as far away as before.
Enemy respawn timers have also also been extended. So, once you've dealt with the
enemies in an area, you should have more time before they return. This should make exploring and gathering
resources a little less hectic, especially when you're trying to focus on a particular task instead of
constantly fighting off another group of enemies. The Scorned Wilderness raid has received
attention as well. Obstacles and enemies should now respawn correctly when you reset the raid or start another run.
The update also fixes an issue where ores could respawn instantly when teleporting in the raid, along with
several wind step related skips. So, there are a few adjustments here aimed at making raid runs behave more
consistently. For ranged equipment, rune arrows and rune bolts now deal more damage than
adamant ammunition, with the listed multipliers being 4.9 times compared with 4.2 times.
That's worth keeping in mind if you're deciding which ammunition to craft and carry into combat.
There's also a long list of smaller fixes affecting skills, crafting stations, equipment effects, quests, and
various activities throughout Ashen Fall. And that brings us to the enormous collection of bug fixes, which covers a
little bit of everything. Players who acquired certain quest items early through multiplayer sessions could
previously find themselves unable to progress into the next region. That's been addressed, so the order in
which you receive those items shouldn't block your progression in the same way. Um there are also fixes for crashing
when selecting online play while offline, rain effects appearing inside player housing, and problems with
ascension cores failing to drop from cauldron in certain circumstances. Interface issues have received plenty of
attention, too. Console players should benefit from fixes for chest sorting and controller navigation,
while UI scaling is now available across all supported platforms as intended. There are corrections for skill menus,
building menus, map navigation, tooltips, and various button prompts. Some players were also experiencing
keyboard freezes after teleporting, and that issue has been addressed. On the visual side, there are fixes for
dragon animations, spell effects, waterfall effects, map fog, and even the rune spade
appearing upside down on a weapons rack. Those little details might not change how you play, but they help the game
feel more polished. There are other fixes aimed specifically at combat and multiplayer.
Enfeeble should now reduce enemy damage correctly across different enemy types. Some problems affecting enchanted bolts
have been resolved, and several boss-related issues have been addressed. This includes situations where Fuz Ro
Dah could become passive or appear to get get back up after being defeated. There are also corrections for dedicated
servers, cross-platform connections, achievements, crafting requirements, and items that weren't behaving properly
after death. Certain key bindings that could potentially leave players stuck in a
soft lock have also had their rebinding options removed, including actions connected to interaction, building,
crafting, and quest dialogue. It might limit a few custom control setups, but the change is intended to prevent
situations where you could accidentally make progress impossible. Now, before we wrap things up, let's
look back at the previous update because that helps explain why this release matters so much.
The previous hotfix focused on preventing world saves from disappearing under certain conditions.
However, it also made clear that worlds which had already vanished from the world list would remain missing until a
later update. At the time, the team was still working on getting those worlds visible again and and finding a way for
players with corrupted character saves to return. This latest release is the follow-up to
that work, bringing further world save fixes and the character recovery option, alongside all the combat additions and
quality of life improvements we've covered. So, while this update doesn't introduce
an entirely new region or a major boss encounter, it addresses some important problems while giving players more ways
to approach combat and manage their adventures. The missing save situation has been a major concern and it's good to see
another step being taken to help affected players get back into the game. There may still be unusual cases that
need attention, but the changes here cover a pretty wide range of issues. With continued support planned for
Ashenfall, along with the announced 2027 roadmap and the Blood Crystal Saga, there's still plenty ahead for Runescape
Dragon Lines. That's all I've got for you guys today. My name is Nico Russell. Thanks for
watching and I'll see you out in Ashenfall.
